lines.2: Sure enough, she brought out rice balls.
lines.4: 「What's this one? Rice wrapped in salmon?」
lines.8: 「Forgive me. Tomorrow, I will make something properly.」
lines.9: 「No, no, it's fine. Don't push yourself.」
lines.10: 「It's not like I expect you to improve overnight.」
lines.13: 「If you have complaints, you may practice cooking yourself.」
lines.14: There it was: the ultimate argument.
lines.15: Only a hero capable of facing ten thousand men could knock this one aside.
lines.16: 「That's a fair point, but can I tell you what I think?」
lines.17: Otome nodded and settled in to listen seriously.
lines.18: But first I needed a lifeline.
lines.20: 「No matter what I say next, you won't get angry.」
lines.21: 「I cannot promise that. If anger is called for, I will be angry.」
lines.22: 「I think this is one of those times when you're supposed to promise even if you have to lie.」
lines.24: 「Very well. As a compromise, I will do my best to be reasonable.」
lines.26: 「I want meals with plenty of variety.」
lines.27: 「But cooking them myself would be a lot of work.」
lines.28: 「In other words, do your best, Otome!」
lines.30: 「...In other words, cooking for yourself is bothersome. But you still want delicious food, so you intend to contribute complaints and nothing else.」
lines.33: I made my voice sound like a needy little brother and looked up at her pleadingly.
lines.34: 「I-It cannot be helped, you spoiled child.」
lines.35: Hah. So much for iron. She was sweeter than chocolate.
lines.36: 「--Did you think I would say that?」
lines.37: ...Looks like I was the one being too sweet.
lines.38: 「Your parents asked me to correct precisely that part of you. It is why I came here.」
